headline: Equities enter Sunday night on the back foot after chips posted their worst week since April 2025 and US-Iran Hormuz tensions kept oil bid.
stance: The prior Friday cash close left the S&P 500 at 7,457.69, down 1.6% on the week, and the Nasdaq at 25,520.24, off 2.9%, with semiconductors entering bear-market territory (–20% from peak). Geopolitical risk in the Strait of Hormuz remains unresolved, keeping WTI crude elevated at $81.77 (prior cash close) and bond yields sticky at the 4.55% area on 10-year Treasuries. The 10-year yield edged lower overnight as traders weighed fresh Middle East strikes against a softer domestic outlook, offering equities a small offset heading into a heavy earnings week.

news.head: Chip bear market
news.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 20% from its record high last week — its worst weekly drop since April 2025 — as investors questioned whether AI spending can justify current valuations.

news.head: TSMC beat, raised capex
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor posted a strong Q2 earnings beat but lifted its full-year capital-expenditure guidance to $60–64 billion (from $52–56 billion prior), which markets read as a cost-inflation signal and pushed the ADR lower.

news.head: US-Iran Hormuz
news.body: The US continued air strikes on Iranian targets through the weekend while Iran warned it would strike regional US allies; the Strait of Hormuz remains under highly stressed military pressure, sustaining the oil-risk premium.

news.head: Netflix disappointed
news.body: Netflix fell more than 8% on Friday after in-line Q2 results and a reduction in viewing-data transparency spooked investors ahead of a extended streaming earnings calendar.

news.head: Moonshot AI shock
news.body: A new large language model from Chinese startup Moonshot surprised the market by claiming performance on par with leading US models, reigniting AI-spending-efficiency concerns across the semiconductor complex.

news.head: Meta-Anthropic compute talks
news.body: Meta is reportedly in early talks to rent computing capacity to Anthropic in a deal that could be worth up to $10 billion, a signal that hyperscaler AI infrastructure buildouts are accelerating even as chip stocks retreat.

news.head: Consumer sentiment rebounds
news.body: The preliminary July University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to 54.4, up nearly 10% from June and well above consensus of 50.5, with the one-year inflation outlook easing to 4.2%.

news.head: This week: INTC, TSLA, Alphabet
news.body: Intel and Tesla report this week alongside Alphabet, whose results will be the first true test of whether hyperscaler AI spending budgets are holding — directly relevant to the chip selloff narrative.

implications: The chip complex entering technical bear-market territory is a drag on the Nasdaq and the broader S&P 500 given semiconductors' record ~20% index weight; sustained selling pressure there keeps the path of least resistance lower for large-cap tech.
Oil held above $80 (WTI prior cash close $81.77; Brent $88.09) despite no confirmed Hormuz closure — a geopolitical risk premium that raises input costs and complicates the Fed's inflation calculus.

June CPI came in at +3.5% year-on-year (below the 3.8% consensus) and PPI fell 0.3%, but resilient retail sales and jobless claims at 208K removed urgency for a July Fed cut; fed-funds futures show roughly 90% odds of a hold at the July 29 meeting.

The 10-year Treasury yield dipped overnight after headlines showed traders weighing fresh Middle East strikes against the domestic outlook — a modest relief valve for equity valuations, but real rates remain elevated at 2.31%.

Positioning: Speculators in Russell 2000 futures are at a 3-year low in bullish bets (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. WTI crude specs are similarly extended short (6th percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean for oil. Copper specs are at the 91st percentile long — a contrarian warning. 2-year Treasury specs are at the 85th percentile long — also a contrarian warning for short-dated rates.

watch.head: Alphabet earnings (Tue)
watch.body: Alphabet is the first hyperscaler to report this cycle; its AI infrastructure spending commentary will either confirm or challenge the chip-selloff narrative that drove last week's losses.

watch.head: INTC and TSLA (this week)
watch.body: Intel and Tesla results arrive mid-week; Intel's foundry progress and Tesla's margin trajectory each carry sector-wide read-throughs.

watch.head: Hormuz headlines
watch.body: Any escalation targeting Iranian energy infrastructure — or a diplomatic opening — would move WTI and Brent sharply and ripple into equity risk appetite; watch for CENTCOM statements overnight.

watch.head: 10Y yield vs 4.55%
watch.body: The 10-year yield closed Friday at 4.55% (prior cash close); a sustained move above 4.60% would tighten financial conditions further and pressure the CAPE 41.5x equity multiple.

watch.head: USD/JPY at 162.35
watch.body: The yen is at a 3-year extreme versus the dollar (prior cash close 162.35, 99th percentile of its 3-year range); any sharp yen strengthening — via Bank of Japan action or risk-off flows — could trigger unwinding of carry trades and hit risk assets broadly.

watch.head: Wheat at 98th percentile
watch.body: Wheat (684.75 c/bu, prior cash close) sits at a 3-year price extreme; combined with corn and soybeans also elevated, food-input inflation is a growing tail risk for consumer staples margins and the broader CPI path.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.55% (prior cash close) and edged lower overnight; the 2-year yield was 4.18% — leaving the yield curve at a modest +37 basis points, which is historically thin for a Fed-on-hold environment.
Real (inflation-adjusted) interest rates stand at 2.31% (prior cash close) — meaningfully positive, which creates ongoing headwinds for growth assets.
The 10-year inflation breakeven sits at 2.24% (prior cash close) — contained relative to the current CPI print, but Hormuz-driven oil at $81.77 is an upside risk.

Fed funds futures price roughly 90% probability of no change at the July 29 FOMC meeting; the June CPI beat (3.5% vs 3.8% expected) and PPI decline of 0.3% provided relief, but 208K jobless claims and solid retail sales prevented a clean dovish repricing.
The MOVE index closed at 70.9 (prior cash close), relatively calm, suggesting the bond market is not in panic mode despite geopolitical noise.
sections.positioning: 3M SOFR futures speculators are at the 3rd percentile of their 3-year range — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for short-dated rate instruments. 2-year Treasury specs sit at the 85th percentile long — speculators are heavily positioned, a contrarian warning for 2-year notes.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: The S&P 500 prior cash close was 7,457.69, down 1.01% Friday and 1.6% on the week; the Nasdaq 100 closed at 25,520.24, off 1.5% Friday and 2.9% on the week.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index entered technical bear-market territory last week, falling 20% from its recent peak — its worst weekly decline since April 2025 — driven by AI-spending valuation concerns and the Moonshot AI model shock.
TSMC's Q2 earnings beat was overshadowed by a capex hike to $60–64 billion from $52–56 billion prior guidance; TSMC ADR shares fell approximately 3.6% in Taiwan on Friday.
Breadth has held up better than the headline indices: 61% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 66.5% above their 200-day (prior cash close).
The VIX closed at 18.77 (prior cash close) — elevated but not at crisis levels; the VXN at 29.03 reflects meaningfully higher anxiety specific to tech.

The SKEW index at 147.3 (prior cash close) indicates the options market is pricing meaningful tail-risk, consistent with elevated geopolitical and earnings uncertainty heading into a heavy reporting week.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 speculators are at the 2nd percentile of their 3-year range — almost no bullish bets remain, a contrarian floor for small-caps. Copper specs sit at the 91st percentile long — a contrarian warning for industrial metals.

sections.title: Commodities & FX
bullets: WTI crude closed at $81.77 (prior cash close) and Brent at $88.09, both sustained by Hormuz tension; WTI specs are at the 6th percentile short — speculators are historically underpositioned for a bullish move, a contrarian lean.
Gold closed at $4,023/oz (prior cash close), near all-time highs, supported by geopolitical uncertainty and central bank buying even as real rates remain at 2.31%.
The DXY dollar index closed at 100.75 (prior cash close); EUR/USD at 1.1446 reflects a relatively soft dollar environment.

USD/JPY at 162.35 (prior cash close, 99th percentile of its 3-year range) is at an extreme; yen-carry unwind risk is elevated — any Bank of Japan hawkish signal or sharp risk-off move could accelerate yen strengthening and pressure global equities.

Wheat at 684.75 c/bu (prior cash close, 98th percentile of its 3-year range) represents a food-inflation tail risk; corn and soybeans are also elevated, adding pressure to consumer staples input costs.
sections.positioning: WTI crude specs are at the 6th percentile short — a contrarian-bullish signal for oil. Wheat specs are at the 90th percentile long — a contrarian warning. GBP specs are at the 6th percentile — speculators are underpositioned long sterling.
